elements: Composite two-panel layout shown together by default: flat uv-parameter plane on the left, curved parametric patch with xyz axes on the right, joined by a curved block arrow

Left panel: black u-axis (horizontal, arrowhead right, italic label 'u') and black v-axis (vertical, arrowhead up, italic label 'v'), origin inside the panel so both axes extend a little into negative territory
Orange vertical line in the uv-plane at u = u0, extending symmetrically below the u-axis and above the top of the plotted region, labeled 'u constant' at its top
Purple/magenta horizontal line in the uv-plane at v = v0, extending symmetrically left of the v-axis and past the right edge, labeled 'v constant' at its right end
Small dot at the crossing point (u0, v0) of the two parameter lines in the uv-plane
Curved pale-yellow block arrow with gray outline sweeping from the right of the uv-plane over to the 3D patch, representing the map r(u,v)

Right panel: 3D coordinate axes drawn as black lines with cone arrowheads — z vertical up (label 'z'), y to screen-right (label 'y'), x toward the lower-left foreground (label 'x'), meeting at a common origin
Smooth doubly-curved light-gray parametric surface patch floating above the xy-plane in the upper-right region of the axes
Curvilinear coordinate grid of thin dark-gray u-curves and v-curves covering the patch (about 5x5 cells), both families visibly bending
Highlighted orange constant-u curve on the surface (image of the orange line), labeled 'Constant u-curve' with a leader line
Highlighted purple/magenta constant-v curve on the surface (image of the purple line), transverse to the orange curve, labeled 'Constant v-curve' with a leader line
Black marker dot at the image point r(u0, v0) where the two highlighted curves cross on the surface

demo_steps.title: The whole picture: domain, map, surface
demo_steps.narration: The default view shows both panels at once: two straight parameter lines crossing in the flat uv-plane, the curved arrow for r(u,v), and their images as two bending curves crossing on the gray patch in xyz-space.

demo_steps.title: Lines in the parameter plane
demo_steps.narration: Look only at the domain. Fixing u = 1.2 gives the vertical orange line; fixing v = 1.2 gives the horizontal purple line. They are perfectly straight and cross at the single parameter pair (u0, v0).

demo_steps.title: Images on the surface
demo_steps.narration: Now look only at the patch. Each straight line is carried onto the curved sheet: the orange constant-u curve and the purple constant-v curve both bend with the surface and meet at the image point r(u0, v0).

demo_steps.title: Sweeping u builds one family
demo_steps.narration: Slide the u value and watch the orange line slide sideways in the domain while its image sweeps across the patch. All those positions together form one family of grid curves.

demo_steps.title: Sweeping v builds the other family
demo_steps.narration: Now slide v. The purple curve sweeps transversally across the patch. The two families overlaid are exactly the curvilinear coordinate grid drawn on the surface.

demo_steps.title: Change the formula
demo_steps.narration: Edit the components — try x = u*cos(v), y = u*sin(v), z = u — and the patch plus both grid families re-form; the domain lines stay straight while their images change shape.

plan.geometry_notes: DEFAULT VIEW is the composite: left uv-panel + curved mapping arrow + right xyz-panel all visible simultaneously, arranged side by side along screen-horizontal, matching the source. LEFT PANEL (flat, always billboarded to face the camera, occupying the left ~35% of the frame): u-axis along screen-right from u = -0.8 to 3.0, v-axis along screen-up from v = -0.8 to 3.0, black lines ~0.03 thick with solid cone arrowheads and italic serif labels 'u' (right end) and 'v' (top). Orange vertical line at u = u0 (default 1.2) drawn from v = -0.6 to v = 2.9 so it crosses and extends symmetrically past the u-axis; purple horizontal line at v = v0 (default 1.2) drawn from u = -0.6 to u = 2.9 so it crosses and extends past the v-axis. Labels 'u constant' set just above the orange line's top end, 'v constant' just above the purple line's right end. Small black dot at (u0, v0). RIGHT PANEL offset about +6 world units in screen-right direction. XYZ ORIENTATION MUST MATCH THE SOURCE: z is world-up and draws vertically up the screen (axis length 3.2); y draws to the screen-right (length 3.2); x recedes toward the LOWER-LEFT FOREGROUND (length 2.6) — i.e. the camera sits roughly over the +x axis, only ~20° toward +y, ~18° above the horizon, so +x points out of the screen toward the viewer's lower-left. Verify this before anything else. DEFAULT SURFACE (curved in BOTH parameter directions): r(u,v) = ⟨u, v, 2.5 - 0.25(u² + v²)⟩ with u ∈ [0.2, 2.2], v ∈ [0.2, 2.2], sampled 48×48. Its z runs from about 2.47 down to 0.08, so the patch is a saddle-free dome-like sheet floating above the first-octant part of the xy-plane, sitting in the UPPER-RIGHT quadrant above the axes exactly as the gray patch is drawn in the source; both constant-u and constant-v curves are visibly parabolic. COLORS: surface fill light gray #CCCCCC, double-sided, slightly translucent, soft top lighting so the near edge reads lighter; surface grid curves dark gray #7A7A7A at ~0.012 thickness, 5 u-curves and 5 v-curves evenly spaced; highlighted constant-u curve orange #F0A030 at ~0.035 thickness; highlighted constant-v curve purple/magenta #B0539E at ~0.035; crossing dot black; axes and label text black; mapping arrow pale yellow fill #FBE3B4 with gray #9A9A9A outline. MAPPING ARROW: thick curved block arrow arcing up and rightward from just right of the uv-panel (screen position ~x=3.4, y=2.0) to the left of the patch (~x=5.4, y=2.6), arrowhead pointing right and slightly down, lying in the screen plane and always camera-facing. Labels 'Constant u-curve' placed to the upper-right beyond the orange curve's high end with a thin leader line, 'Constant v-curve' to the right of the patch beyond the purple curve's end with a leader line.
plan.notes: Build the patch with ParametricGeometry rebuilt whenever an equation field changes; parse the three component strings at runtime (math.js or small recursive-descent parser) with variables u and v, reporting parse errors inline under the offending field while keeping the last valid surface. Grid curves and the two highlighted curves are separate TubeGeometry/Line2 objects sampled from the same parsed functions, offset ~0.01 along the surface normal to avoid z-fighting. On re-parse, recompute the patch bounding box and re-fit the zoom so exotic formulas stay framed, but do NOT change the camera's azimuth/elevation. The toggle only fades groups in/out and re-centers framing: 'Both (mapping)' keeps all three groups at the composite framing (initial state), 'uv-domain only' zooms to the flat panel face-on, 'xyz-surface only' zooms to the patch keeping the source orientation. Orbit affects only the xyz group and is disabled in the uv-only view; clamp elevation to 0-60° so z stays up. Labels ('u', 'v', 'x', 'y', 'z', 'u constant', 'v constant', 'Constant u-curve', 'Constant v-curve') as camera-facing sprites or HTML overlays in italic serif for variables. Flat white background, no ground plane or shadows, to keep the textbook line-art look.

authoredPrompt: This figure illustrates how constant-parameter lines in the uv-parameter domain map to curves on a parametric surface in 3D space. Left panel: the uv-plane showing a vertical orange line labeled u constant and a horizontal purple line labeled v constant. Right panel: a smooth curved parametric patch in xyz-space, with a constant u-curve highlighted in orange and a constant v-curve highlighted in purple on the surface; families of such curves form the curvilinear coordinate grid covering the surface. An arrow connects the two panels to indicate the mapping. The figure establishes that fixing one parameter in a parametric surface equation produces a curve on the surface, and that families of u-curves and v-curves together form the natural coordinate grid on a parametric surface.
authoredInteractions:
- equation input for the parametric surface: three fields for x(u,v), y(u,v), z(u,v) pre-filled with a simple example (e.g. x=u*cos(v), y=u*sin(v), z=u); when the learner edits any component the 3D surface redraws and the constant-u and constant-v grid curves update — shows how the algebraic form of r(u,v) determines the surface geometry and the shape of the parameter curves
- sliders for u and v: sweep the highlighted constant-u (orange) and constant-v (pink) curves across the surface
authoredContext: We have seen that curves in 3-space can be represented by three equations involving one parameter, say x = x(t), y = y(t), z = z(t) Surfaces in 3-space can be represented parametrically by three equations involving two parameters, say x = x(u, v), y = y(u, v), z = z(u, v) (3) To visualize why such equations represent a surface, think of (u, v) as a point that varies over some region in a uv-plane. If u is held constant, then v is the only varying parameter in (3), and hence these equations represent a curve in 3-space. We call this a constant u-curve (Figure 14.4.5). Similarly, if v is held constant, then u is the only varying parameter in (3), so again these equations represent a curve in 3-space. We call this a constant v-curve. By varying the constants we generate a family of u-curves and a family of v-curves that together form a surface.
sourceQmd: Anton, Bivens, and Davis. Calculus, 10th Edition, Figure 14.4.5

Orange vertical line at u = u0 (default 1.2) spanning v = 0 to 2.4, label 'u constant' just above its top. Purple horizontal line at v = v0 (default 0.8) spanning u = 0 to 2.6, label 'v constant' above its right end. Default surface r(u,v) = ⟨u·cos v, u·sin v, u⟩ with u ∈ [0.4, 2], v ∈ [0, π/2], sampled 40×40; it renders as a gently curved quadrilateral sheet occupying the upper-right region above the axes' origin, about 2 units across and floating ~1–3 units above the xy-plane, exactly as the gray patch sits in the source. Surface fill light gray #CCCCCC (double-sided, slightly translucent, soft top lighting so the near edge reads lighter than the far edge); coordinate grid lines on the surface dark gray #7A7A7A, 4 u-curves and 4 v-curves, thin (~0.012). Highlighted constant-u curve (v varying) in orange #F0A030, thickness ~0.035, running from the front-lower-left of the patch to the back-upper-right; highlighted constant-v curve (u varying) in purple/magenta #B0539E, same thickness, running roughly left-to-right across the patch and crossing the orange curve. Small black dot at the crossing point. Labels: 'Constant u-curve' at the upper right beyond the orange curve's top end; 'Constant v-curve' on two lines at the right edge beyond the purple curve. MAPPING ARROW: pale yellow fill #FBE3B4 with gray #9A9A9A outline, a thick curved block arrow arcing up and over from just right of the uv-plane (~x=3.2, y=1.8) to the left edge of the surface panel (~x=4.6, y=2.4), arrowhead pointing right-down toward the surface; it lies in the screen plane, always facing the camera.
interactionPlan.notes: Build the surface with a ParametricGeometry rebuilt whenever an equation field or the u/v domain changes; parse the three component strings at runtime (math.js or a small recursive-descent parser) with variables u, v, and show parse errors inline under the offending field while keeping the last valid surface. Grid curves and the two highlighted curves are separate TubeGeometry/Line2 objects sampled from the same parsed functions so they always hug the surface (offset outward by ~0.01 along the normal to avoid z-fighting). Auto-fit the camera/zoom to the surface bounding box after each re-parse so exotic formulas stay in frame. Labels ('u', 'v', 'x', 'y', 'z', 'u constant', 'v constant', 'Constant u-curve', 'Constant v-curve') as camera-facing sprites/HTML overlays in a serif math italic for variables. The panel toggle cross-fades the uv-plane group and the xyz group and animates the camera between a front-on framing (uv only) and the standard isometric pose (surface only); 'Both' pulls back to show the pair with the mapping arrow. Orbit is limited to the xyz group; when in uv-only view lock orbit to the flat front view. Use a flat white background and no ground plane, matching the textbook's line-art look.

discrepancies: Default state shows only the uv-parameter plane; the source figure is a single composite showing the uv-plane, the curved mapping arrow, and the xyz surface together — the 'Both (mapping)' view should be the initial state so the figure is recognizable at a glance.

The chosen surface r = ⟨u cos v, u sin v, u⟩ is a cone patch, so constant-v curves are perfectly straight rulings; the source patch is a doubly-curved sheet where both families bend, which reads more clearly as a general parametric surface.

In the uv-plane, the orange u-constant line starts at the u-axis and only extends upward, and the purple line barely extends left of the v-axis; in the source both lines extend well past the axes in both directions.

The source's orange/purple curves on the surface run edge-to-edge across the visible patch with the labels placed just outside the patch boundary; the generated highlight curve endpoints and label anchors follow the parameter domain edges, which may place labels inconsistently as sliders move.
Mapping block arrow is only present in the 'Both' view (correct behaviour once that view is default, but absent in the screenshot).
evaluation.notes: Conceptually solid and richly interactive (view toggles, u/v sliders, editable parametrization, guided demo), but the default state shows only the flat uv-plane so the figure initially looks like a 2D plot rather than the source's uv→xyz mapping composite, and the cone parametrization yields straight rulings instead of the source's doubly-curved patch.
action_items: Make 'Both (mapping)' the initial view so the uv-plane, curved arrow, and 3D surface appear together like the source.
Use a default surface with curvature in both parameter directions (e.g. z = 1 - 0.25(u²+v²) over a rectangular domain) so both constant-u and constant-v curves visibly bend as in the source.
Extend the orange and purple parameter lines symmetrically past the u- and v-axes in the uv-plane to match the source's crossing lines.
Verify the xyz camera reproduces the source orientation (z up, y to the right, x toward the lower-left foreground) and that the patch sits in the upper-right quadrant above the axes as drawn.
plan_action_items: Specify the composite 'both panels + mapping arrow' layout as the default view state rather than a single panel.

feedback.rationale: The critic's core issues are structural plan choices — the default view should be the composite 'both panels + mapping arrow' state and the default parametrization should be a doubly-curved patch rather than a cone — which must be respecified in the plan before implementation details are polished.

plan.notes: Build the patch with ParametricGeometry rebuilt whenever an equation field changes; parse the three component strings at runtime (math.js or small recursive-descent parser) with variables u and v, reporting parse errors inline under the offending field while keeping the last valid surface. Grid curves and the two highlighted curves are separate TubeGeometry/Line2 objects sampled from the same parsed functions, offset ~0.01 along the surface normal to avoid z-fighting. Labels ('u', 'v', 'x', 'y', 'z', 'u constant', 'v constant', 'Constant u-curve', 'Constant v-curve') as camera-facing sprites or HTML overlays in italic serif for variables. Flat white background, no ground plane or shadows, to keep the textbook line-art look.

demo_steps.title: The whole picture: domain, map, surface
demo_steps.narration: The default view shows both panels at once: two straight parameter lines crossing in the flat uv-plane, the curved arrow for r(u,v), and their images as two bending curves crossing on the gray patch in xyz-space.

demo_steps.title: Lines in the parameter plane
demo_steps.narration: Look only at the domain. Fixing u = 1.2 gives the vertical orange line; fixing v = 1.2 gives the horizontal purple line. They are perfectly straight and cross at the single parameter pair (u0, v0).

demo_steps.title: Images on the surface
demo_steps.narration: Now look only at the patch. Each straight line is carried onto the curved sheet: the orange constant-u curve and the purple constant-v curve both bend with the surface and meet at the image point r(u0, v0).

demo_steps.title: Sweeping u builds one family
demo_steps.narration: Slide the u value and watch the orange line slide sideways in the domain while its image sweeps across the patch. All those positions together form one family of grid curves.

demo_steps.title: Sweeping v builds the other family
demo_steps.narration: Now slide v. The purple curve sweeps transversally across the patch. The two families overlaid are exactly the curvilinear coordinate grid drawn on the surface.

demo_steps.title: Change the formula
demo_steps.narration: Edit the components — try x = u*cos(v), y = u*sin(v), z = u — and the patch plus both grid families re-form; the domain lines stay straight while their images change shape.
